title: Nitrate and phosphate rose with AOU and winter saturation did not fall, so the sigma0 26.5 O2 loss in the western North Pacific is regenerated; off California nitrate explains 65% (1984-2025)
abstract: Question: is the sigma0 26.5 oxygen (O2) loss at its western North Pacific source a change of preformed O2 (water that leaves the winter mixed layer with less O2) or a regenerated change (water that holds more respired matter)? Approach: we used all World Ocean Database bottle casts with O2 and nutrients in 15-50 N, 140 E-110 W (1950-2025). We calculated within-water-type changes of AOU, nitrate and phosphate (2009-2025 and 1997-2008 minus 1984-1996) with a fixed-effects model and a joint cruise bootstrap. The regenerated fraction f is R x d(nutrient)/dAOU (O2:N:P = 150:16:1). The decision rule (f interval above 0.5 = regenerated) was fixed before the nutrient changes were computed. We also measured O2 saturation of winter mixed layers of the sigma0 26.3-26.7 class (ship bottles 1950-2025, BGC-Argo floats). Results: in 28-46 N, 140 E-180 (151 and 62 cruises), AOU rose by 17.6 umol/kg (12.1 to 21.0) and nitrate by 2.50 (1.63 to 3.06), so f = 1.34 (1.06 to 1.69); for phosphate f = 1.43 (1.04 to 1.75). Five western sub-regions gave f = 1.02-1.53. Removing per-cruise offsets on deep surfaces gave f = 1.77; GLODAP cruises alone gave 1.06 (0.25 to 1.84). Winter mixed-layer saturation was 98.0% in 1984-1996 (52 cruises), 98.4% in 1997-2008 and 99.7% in 2009-2025 (5 cruises), so preformed O2 did not fall (1997-2008 change +1.4 umol/kg, -4.5 to +7.2). Off southern California (69 and 40 cruises), f = 0.65 (0.60 to 0.71) for nitrate and 0.74 for phosphate; -6.0 umol/kg (-7.0 to -5.0) of the O2 loss has no matching nitrate, and this gap opened after 2008. Interpretation: the shrinking winter outcrop of this class acts through renewal (older water or more respiration), not through lower preformed O2. The O2 loss that models miss must come from ventilation and respiration, not from air-sea gas exchange. Nutrients rose more than AOU in the west, which suggests higher preformed nutrients as the outcrop moved north. Limitations: WOD nutrients are not calibrated between cruises; the 160 E-180 core, the offshore east and the California check have few cruises; the post-2008 saturation rests on 5 cruises; floats cannot test the trend because of their calibration history; f near 1 does not separate older water from faster respiration.
